mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, I want you to remember—walking forward in faith isn’t about having everything figured out. It’s about living the questions, and letting the story unfold, even when it’s messy or uncertain. If you’ve come this far, you already know: real faith is about wrestling with the biggest questions—about suffering, justice, meaning, and hope. And you’ve realized by now that doubt isn’t a weakness. It’s a sign you’re being honest, that you care enough to ask the hard questions. Along this journey, you’ve caught a glimpse of a story that’s both ancient and new—one that invites you to see the world, and yourself, in a whole new light. So, what are the big things to carry with you? Doubt and faith often walk side by side. That longing you feel for justice, for meaning—those aren’t just random thoughts. They point beyond what we can measure. Forgiveness? It’s powerful. It breaks the cycle of hurt and lets healing in. And community—don’t forget that. We’re not meant to go it alone. Faith is something we live out together. Most of all, the invitation isn’t about certainty. It’s about trust, even when you can’t see the whole path ahead. Here’s what this means for you: you’re never alone in your questions. This story of faith isn’t about having all the answers. It’s about taking the next step, even if you’re not sure where it’ll lead. Whether you’re brimming with hope or weighed down by doubt, there’s space for you here. You don’t have to leave your questions or your fears behind. Bring your whole self—every part of you belongs on this journey. Real change shows up right in the middle of struggle, not when everything is easy. If you find yourself longing for meaning, for justice, for a love that lasts—those are more than dreams. They’re signposts, nudging you home. The road might be long. Sometimes it’s hard. But you don’t have to walk it by yourself. So, take courage. Keep asking. Let your story keep unfolding. The world needs people who are willing to live with hope, to forgive, to search for truth, and to love deeply. That’s the invitation in front of you. That’s the adventure of faith.
